/benchmarks.title: LLM Benchmarks Explained: What Each Test Measures | Pairvu
description: Every LLM benchmark on Pairvu explained — what it measures, which exact model versions were tested, and when each result was published.
/benchmarks.mainText: Benchmark index · updated 2026-11-16 LLM benchmarks A benchmark score is meaningful only with its version, harness, model configuration, and source. Pairvu does not combine unrelated harnesses into a composite score. Pairvu currently explains two benchmarks. The owner publication date, model-owner report date, and Pairvu collection date describe different events; a recent source check does not make an older result new. What each test measures CursorBench 4.0: coding agents in a real editor Cursor evaluates coding agents on ambiguous, multi-file tasks drawn from real Cursor sessions; higher scores are better. Version 4.0 introduced long-horizon tasks on 2026-09-10 , including editing, refactoring, investigation, and design adherence. Pairvu preserves Gemini 4 Carbon High, Fable 5.2 Max, Opus 5.5 Max, and Haiku 5.5 Max, with each configuration and owner-reported cost per task. Individual result publication dates are not stated on the cited leaderboard. Pairvu checked this snapshot on 2026-11-16 ; that is a collection date. Results depend on the exact model, effort setting, Cursor agent harness, and task budget. Small score gaps may reflect run variance and should not be treated as universal model quality. BrowseComp: persistent information search BrowseComp tests whether an agent can persistently locate hard-to-find facts. Its questions have short, verifiable answers and were designed to resist simple search. The original 2025-04-10 release contains 1,266 questions. Pairvu shows its Deep research, o1, GPT-4o with browsing, and GPT-4.5 baselines separately from Z.ai's 2026-02-12 GLM-5 report. The GLM-5 thinking and context-management configurations are distinct. Neither source supplies per-task run cost for the displayed results. Short-answer accuracy does not represent the full distribution of open-ended browsing work. Test-time compute, browsing tools, aggregation, and context management can materially change results. BrowseComp-Plus, named in some model launch reports, is a different evaluation and is not substituted here. Coverage matrix Benchmark Version / date Pairvu coverage Configuration and cost Main limitation CursorBench v 4.0 · version introduced 2026-09-10 Snapshot checked 2026-11-16 Individual result publication dates unknown This Pairvu snapshot shows four named configurations from the owner leaderboard; it is not the full leaderboard. Named effort configurations; owner-reported run cost per task. Cursor agent harness and task budget are part of the result. BrowseComp BrowseComp original release (1,266 tasks) Owner release 2025-04-10 Z.ai report 2026-02-12 Pairvu preserves four OpenAI release baselines and two later GLM-5 vendor-reported configurations; these are separate evidence sets. Baseline and vendor configurations are separate; cited sources do not report run cost. Short-answer browsing tasks are not a universal measure of open-ended research.
